3-day-kakheti-wine-and-food-tour-from-tb.title: 3-Day Kakheti Wine and Food Tour from Tbilisi
3-day-kakheti-wine-and-food-tour-from-tb.description:
The 3-Day Kakheti Wine and Food Tour is a private trip from Tbilisi through Kakheti, Georgia's main wine region in the South Caucasus. Over three days you taste at both family-run wineries and larger wine estates, see the qvevri method that UNESCO recognizes as intangible cultural heritage, and visit the region's cultural landmarks — Tsinandali Estate, Gremi Fortress, the hilltop town of Sighnaghi and Bodbe Monastery — with traditional Georgian meals paired with local wine.

Three days is enough to go well beyond a day trip at a balanced pace, with tastings alongside food, old towns and quiet cultural sites — so it suits wine lovers and first-time visitors to Kakheti alike, on its own or as part of a longer route through Georgia. You stay two nights in Telavi, in the heart of the region, so daily drives stay short and you unpack once. Along the way you meet two kinds of producer: family wineries, where wine is still made in buried qvevri and hosted around a home table, and larger estates such as Tsinandali and Khareba — a contrast that's part of what makes the three days interesting.

Because it's private, the tour runs only for your group, with your own guide-driver, and the route, hotels and pace can be shaped around what you want. Hikasus Travel is a local team based in Georgia and handles the transport, hotels, guiding and logistics, so you can focus on the wine, food and the drive.
3-day-kakheti-wine-and-food-tour-from-tb.listingDescription: A private 3-day wine and culture tour of Kakheti from Tbilisi — qvevri winemaking, up to 6 tastings, and cultural stops at Tsinandali, Gremi, Sighnaghi and Bodbe, with hotels, transport and a guide-driver handled for you.
highlights: Private three-day route from Tbilisi into Kakheti, Georgia's main wine region
Six wine tastings across family wineries and larger estates
Qvevri winemaking — the UNESCO-listed method of fermenting wine in buried clay vessels
A tasting inside Khareba Winery's underground tunnels
Cultural stops at Tsinandali Estate, Telavi, Gremi Fortress, Sighnaghi and Bodbe Monastery
Traditional Georgian meals paired with regional wine
Scenic drives over the Gombori Pass and through the Alazani Valley
Two nights in a Telavi hotel, in your choice of comfort level

itinerary.title: Day 1 — Tbilisi - Telavi - Tsinandali Estate - Local Winery - Telavi
itinerary.content:
You leave Tbilisi behind and cross into Kakheti over the Gombori Pass, visit the Tsinandali Estate, and have lunch and a tasting at a family winery before settling into Telavi for two nights.

You leave Tbilisi in the morning and head east into Kakheti over the Gombori Pass, a mountain road that eases you into the region's rural landscapes. Around midday you reach the Tsinandali Estate, a 19th-century estate with landscaped gardens, its own winery and a long winemaking history. From there you stop at a family-run winery for a traditional Georgian lunch paired with wines made on site. In the evening you arrive in Telavi and check in for the first of two nights.

  • Drive over the Gombori Pass into Kakheti;
  • Visit the Tsinandali Estate and its gardens;
  • Lunch and wine tasting at a family-run winery;
  • Overnight stay in Telavi.
  • Duration of the tour: 7-8 hours
  • Driving duration: 2.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 2 — Telavi - Vardisubani - Khareba Winery - Gremi - Napareuli - Telavi
itinerary.content:
A full day of traditional winemaking and local culture: qvevri wine in Vardisubani, a tasting in Khareba's rock-cut tunnels, the medieval Gremi Fortress, and a home-style dinner in Napareuli.

The day starts in the village of Vardisubani, where families still ferment wine in qvevris — large clay vessels set into the ground — for a close look at a method that goes back thousands of years. Next is Khareba Winery, where the tasting takes place inside tunnels carved into the rock. You then visit Gremi Fortress, a 16th-century royal citadel that overlooks the Alazani Valley. The day closes in the village of Napareuli with a traditional dinner and locally made wine, before you return to your hotel in Telavi.

  • Qvevri winemaking in Vardisubani;
  • Wine tasting in Khareba Winery's underground tunnels;
  • Visit Gremi Fortress;
  • Dinner with local wine in Napareuli;
  • Overnight stay in Telavi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 2 hours

itinerary.title: Day 3 — Telavi - Batonistsikhe - Sighnaghi - Bodbe - Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
Your last day takes in Batonistsikhe Castle in Telavi, the hilltop town of Sighnaghi and Bodbe Monastery, with a final tasting before the drive back to Tbilisi.

You begin at Batonistsikhe Castle, a former royal residence in Telavi, with time to walk through the town. From there you drive to Sighnaghi, a walled hilltop town of cobbled streets and painted houses known as the "City of Love," with wide views over the Alazani Valley. Nearby is Bodbe Monastery, a quiet complex set among cypress trees. Before heading back, you share a final dinner and wine tasting at a local winery, then return to Tbilisi.

  • Visit Batonistsikhe Castle and walk through Telavi;
  • Visit Sighnaghi;
  • Visit Bodbe Monastery;
  • Final dinner and wine tasting at a local winery;
  • Return to Tbilisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 10-11 hours
  • Driving duration: 4 hours

included: Two nights' accommodation in Telavi, double/twin sharing, with breakfast
Six wine tastings, one lunch and two dinners

Arrive in Tbilisi. Meet your driver and head to your hotel to check in.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Tbilisi city tour
itinerary.content:
Lose yourself in the captivating charm of Tbilisi's Old Town – a fairytale setting of cobblestone streets and historic architecture. Imagine yourself soaking in therapeutic sulfur baths, the ancient secrets of the city swirling around you. Explore the vibrant Rustaveli Avenue, the heart of modern Tbilisi, and admire the architectural splendor of Freedom Square and the Peace Bridge. Conclude your day with a delightful dinner, savoring the authentic flavors of Georgian cuisine.

itinerary.title: Day 3: Tbilisi – Jvari – Mtskheta – Ananuri – Kazbegi
itinerary.content:
Step back in time to Mtskheta, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, then marvel at the stunning Ananuri fortress before arriving in breathtaking Kazbegi, nestled amidst majestic peaks. Prepare to be awestruck!

itinerary.title: Day 4: Kazbegi
itinerary.content:
Conquer the trails leading to the iconic Gergeti Trinity Church, a masterpiece perched high in the mountains, with panoramic views that will steal your breath away. Feel the raw power of nature in the Gveleti waterfalls and the dramatic Dariali Gorge.

  • Visit Gergeti Trinity Church;
  • Gveleti waterfalls;
  • Dariali Gorge.
  • Duration of the tour: 6-7 hours
  • Driving duration: 1 hour

itinerary.title: Day 5: Kazbegi – Stalin Museum in Gori – Uplistsikhe - Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
A Day of Contrasts – From Stalin's Legacy to Ancient Wonders. Experience a fascinating juxtaposition of history today, starting with a visit to the Stalin Museum in Gori. Reflect on the complex legacy of this controversial figure, before embarking on a journey to the utterly different world of Uplistsikhe, an ancient cave town etched into the landscape. This extraordinary site offers a breathtaking contrast to the museum, revealing the enduring spirit of Georgia's past. Conclude your day back in the bustling capital, Tbilisi, where ancient echoes blend seamlessly with modern life.

  • Check out of the hotel in Kazbegi;
  • Visit Stalin Museum in Gori;
  • Uplistsikhe cave town;
  • Overnight in Tbilisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 9-10 hours
  • Driving duration: 5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 6: Tbilisi - Chiatura - Lunch at Lia - Katskhi pillar - Kutaisi
itinerary.content:
Unique Georgia – From Cable Cars to Ancient Pillars. Today's journey takes you to Chiatura, where you'll experience a unique cable car ride offering breathtaking views. Enjoy a memorable family-style lunch at Lia, savoring the flavors of Georgia before witnessing the awe-inspiring Katskhi Pillar, a solitary rock formation standing tall through centuries. Finally, arrive in Kutaisi, get ready for a relaxing evening.

  • Drive to Chiatura;
  • Lunch at Georgian family;
  • Visit Katskhi Pillar;
  • Overnight stay in Kutaisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 3.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 7: Kutaisi – Prometheus cave – Martvili Canyon – Kutaisi
itinerary.content:
Today's adventure takes you to two of Georgia's most stunning natural wonders. Begin by descending into the mesmerizing Prometheus Cave, a subterranean world of stalactites and stalagmites, where the earth reveals its hidden artistry. Afterward, journey to Martvili Canyon, where you'll traverse well-maintained trails, taking in the breathtaking views of this verdant gorge. Gaze up at the towering cliffs, breathe in the fresh mountain air, and let the serenity of the canyon wash over you. Return to Kutaisi.

  • Visit Prometheus Cave Natural Monument;
  • Martvili Canyon, boat trip;
  • Free evening; Overnight stay in Kutaisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 2.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 8: Kutaisi – Baia's Winery – Batumi
itinerary.content:
A Relaxing Journey to the Coast. Enjoy a relaxing start to the day with a visit to a local family winery. Savor the flavors of Georgian wine before embarking on a scenic journey towards the stunning coastal city of Batumi. Look forward to exploring Batumi's attractions. Overnight stay in Batumi.

  • Check out of the hotel in Kutaisi;
  • Lunch and wine tasting at Baia's Winery;
  • Free evening; Overnight stay in Batumi.
  • Duration of the tour: 7-8 hours
  • Driving duration: 3.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 9: Batumi city tour - Batumi Botanical Garden, free evening
itinerary.content:
Explore Batumi's captivating city center, admiring the architectural highlights of Europe Square, Piazza Square, and the iconic Ali and Nino Statue. Take a memorable cable car ride offering panoramic views, and explore the lush beauty of the Batumi Botanical Garden. Enjoy your free time soaking in the Batumi atmosphere.

  • Piazza Square;
  • Ali and Nino Statue;
  • Enjoy a cable car ride;
  • Batumi Botanical Garden;
  • Free evening in Batumi.

itinerary.title: Day 10: Batumi – Tbilisi (train)
itinerary.content:
Enjoy a relaxing morning in Batumi before checking out and boarding the evening train to Tbilisi. Enjoy a scenic journey through Georgia's diverse landscape.

  • At 16:00, transfer to the train station. The train departs at 16:55 and arrives in Tbilisi at 22:15. Overnight stay in Tbilisi.
  • Batumi-Tbilisi train: 5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 11: Tbilisi – Telavi – Tsinandali – Lunch and wine tasting at the winery – Telavi
itinerary.content:
Embark on a journey to the heart of Georgia's wine region, Kakheti. Explore the charming town of Telavi, visit the historic Tsinandali Estate, and indulge in a delightful lunch and wine tasting at a local winery.

  • Visit Tsinandali Estate;
  • Lunch and wine tasting at the winery;

  • Driving duration: 2.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 12: Telavi – Bodbe – Sighnaghi – Dinner and wine tasting at a winery – Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
Explore more of Kakheti's treasures today, including the Bodbe Monastery and the picturesque town of Sighnaghi, known as the "City of Love." Enjoy a final dinner and wine tasting before returning to Tbilisi.

  • Check out of the hotel in Telavi;
  • Explore Telavi, including a visit to the monument of Erekle II and an excursion to the Telavi Historical Museum (Batonistsikhe);
  • Visit Bodbe and explore Sighnaghi, the city of love;
  • Enjoy dinner and wine tasting at a winery;
  • Drive to Tbilisi for an overnight stay.
  • Duration of the tour: 9-10 hours

itinerary.title: Day 13: Free Day in Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
Today is a free day to enjoy Tbilisi at your own pace. You may choose to explore the Old Town further, visit museums, relax in the famous sulfur baths, or discover local cafés and restaurants.

Recommended places to visit in Tbilisi during your free day:

  • Mtatsminda Park – Located on a hill above the city, this park offers panoramic views over Tbilisi and a relaxed atmosphere with cafés and walking paths.
  • Bazaar on Orbeliani – A modern food and shopping complex where you can buy local products such as Georgian cheese, wine, spices, and traditional sweets.
  • Tbilisi Botanical Garden – A peaceful green space in the heart of the city, ideal for a walk among plants, waterfalls, and scenic viewpoints.
  • Georgian National Museum – A great place to learn more about the country's history, archaeology, and culture.
  • Dry Bridge Market – A famous open-air flea market where you can find antiques, Soviet memorabilia, old cameras, and unique souvenirs.
  • Rustaveli Avenue – Tbilisi's main boulevard, lined with historic buildings, theatres, cafés, and shops.
  • Old Tbilisi wine bars and souvenir shops – A perfect area to enjoy Georgian wine, local cuisine, and traditional handmade crafts.

itinerary.title: Day 14: Departure – Farewell Georgia
itinerary.content:
After a final Georgian breakfast, it's time to depart from Tbilisi International Airport, taking with you unforgettable memories of your Georgian adventure.

  • Check out of the hotel till noon. Transfer to Tbilisi International Airport.

5-day-private-tour-from-tbilisi-to-batum.title: 5-Day Private Tour from Tbilisi to Batumi
5-day-private-tour-from-tbilisi-to-batum.description:
West to the sea in five days. This private tour runs from Tbilisi across Georgia's historic heartland to Kutaisi and the Black Sea at Batumi, then back to the capital — a lot of the country in a short, easy loop.

The first day covers the big sights between the two cities: the hilltop Jvari monastery, the old capital of Mtskheta, the cave town of Uplistsikhe and the Stalin Museum in Gori, ending in Kutaisi. Two nights there give you the Gelati and Motsameta monasteries, the Green Bazaar and the Prometheus Cave, before the road drops to Batumi for two nights on the coast.

Batumi is the payoff — a seaside city of botanical gardens, palm-lined boulevards and modern towers, with a full day to take it in before the drive back east. It's a good first trip for anyone who wants more than the capital without a long itinerary.

The first and last days carry some real driving, but the middle of the trip is relaxed — and because it's private, the pace and the stops bend around you.

Explore Mtskheta and the UNESCO-listed Svetitskhoveli Cathedral
Discover Uplistsikhe, one of Georgia's oldest cave cities
Visit the Stalin Museum in Gori
Experience Kutaisi, including the medieval Gelati Monastery
Walk through the lively Kutaisi Green Bazaar
Explore the underground halls of Prometheus Cave
Travel from inland Georgia to the Black Sea coast

itinerary.title: Day 1: Tbilisi – Jvari – Uplistsikhe – Gori – Kutaisi
itinerary.content:
Your journey begins with a morning pick-up in Tbilisi and a drive toward Georgia's ancient heartland. First is Jvari Monastery, perched above the confluence of the Aragvi and Mtkvari rivers, then Mtskheta and the UNESCO-listed Svetitskhoveli Cathedral. Carry on to Gori for the Stalin Museum, in the town where he was born, and Uplistsikhe, one of Georgia's oldest cave towns carved into the cliffs, before arriving in Kutaisi for the night.

  • Visit Jvari Monastery;
  • Explore Mtskheta and Svetitskhoveli Cathedral (UNESCO World Heritage Site);
  • Visit the Stalin Museum in Gori;
  • Visit Uplistsikhe cave town;
  • Overnight stay in Kutaisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 10-11 hours
  • Driving duration: 5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 2: Kutaisi – Motsameta – Gelati – Kutaisi
itinerary.content:
A relaxed day around Kutaisi. You'll visit Motsameta Monastery, set on a cliff above the Tskhaltsitela River, and Gelati, founded in the 12th century and on the UNESCO list, its churches lined with medieval mosaics and frescoes. Afterwards you'll walk through the Kutaisi Green Bazaar, with free time to see more of the city at your own pace.

  • Visit Motsameta Monastery;
  • Visit Gelati Monastery (UNESCO World Heritage Site);
  • Walk through the Kutaisi Green Bazaar;
  • Free time in Kutaisi;
  • Overnight stay in Kutaisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 4-5 hours
  • Driving duration: 1 hour

itinerary.title: Day 3: Kutaisi – Prometheus Cave – Musicians Park – Batumi
itinerary.content:
Today you travel from Kutaisi to the Black Sea coast, starting underground at the Prometheus Cave, with its stalactites, stalagmites and underground river — including an optional boat ride when it's operating. Continuing west, if open, you'll stop at the Musicians Park in Shekvetili before reaching Batumi, where the rest of the day is free for the beach or the seaside boulevard.

  • Visit Prometheus Cave, with an optional boat ride if operating;
  • Stop at Musicians Park if open (closed Mondays and Thursdays);
  • Overnight stay in Batumi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 3.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 4: Batumi City Tour
itinerary.content:
A relaxed day on the coast. You'll start north of the city at the Batumi Botanical Garden, a hillside of plants from all over the world spread across a green headland above the sea. Back in town, you'll take in Europe Square and the Italianate Piazza, then head down to the water for the moving Ali and Nino statue, two steel figures that slide through each other by the shore, and the Alphabetic Tower nearby, its tall helix wrapped in the letters of the Georgian alphabet. From there it's a stroll along the seafront Batumi Boulevard and a ride up on the Argo cable car for the view over the city and the coast. The evening is free.

  • Visit the Batumi Botanical Garden;
  • Walk through Europe Square and Piazza Square;
  • See the Ali and Nino statue;
  • See the Alphabetic Tower;
  • Walk along Batumi Boulevard;
  • Ride the Argo cable car;
  • Overnight stay in Batumi.
  • Duration of the tour: 5-6 hours
  • Driving duration: 1 hour

itinerary.content:
Check out of your hotel by 12:00 p.m. At 16:00 you'll be transferred to Batumi Railway Station for the 16:50 train to Tbilisi — a scenic ride of about four hours across the country, arriving at 20:50, where your five-day journey comes to an end.

5-day-georgia-private-tour-tbilisi-wine-.title: 5-Day Georgia Private Tour: Tbilisi, Wine & Sulfur Baths
5-day-georgia-private-tour-tbilisi-wine-.description:
Mountains and wine in five days. This private loop from Tbilisi pairs the high Caucasus with the country's oldest wine region — monasteries and snow peaks one day, cellars and vineyards the next.

It opens gently in the capital, with a walk through the Old Town and a look at the sulfur bath district the city grew up around. Then you head north on the Georgian Military Highway, climbing past the monasteries of Mtskheta and the fortress at Ananuri to Kazbegi, a small town beneath the snows of Mount Kazbek and the lone church at Gergeti — the view most people picture when they think of Georgia.

From there it's east into Kakheti, where Georgians have made wine in clay for 8,000 years. You'll taste it at a grand old estate and inside a cellar tunnelled into a mountain, wander the walled hill town of Sighnaghi above the Alazani valley, and end back in Tbilisi.

The days are full and the driving is real, but each evening lands you somewhere new — and because it's private, the whole thing bends around you rather than the other way round.

itinerary.title: Day 1: Arrival and city tour in Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
You'll be met at the airport and taken to your hotel. Check-in is from 14:00, so if you arrive earlier, we'll begin the city tour first and settle you in afterwards. Either way, the tour starts at Holy Trinity Cathedral — Sameba — one of the largest Orthodox churches in the world, rising above the city. From there you'll visit the clifftop Metekhi church, perched above the river, then ride the cable car up to the Narikala fortress for the view over the whole of Tbilisi. Walking down from the fortress, you'll pass through Abanotubani, the district of brick-domed sulfur bathhouses the city was built on and named after, then wander the Old Town lanes to the leaning clock tower of the Rezo Gabriadze theatre. After the tour, you'll have free time until the evening. The day ends with a welcome dinner of Georgian food and local wine.

  • Arrival in Tbilisi and hotel check-in;
  • Visit Holy Trinity Cathedral (Sameba);
  • See Metekhi Church;
  • Ride the cable car to Narikala Fortress;
  • Walk through the Abanotubani sulfur bath district;
  • See the Rezo Gabriadze Theatre clock tower;
  • Walk across the Peace Bridge;
  • Welcome dinner in Tbilisi;
  • Overnight stay in Tbilisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 4-5 hours
  • Driving duration: 30 minutes

itinerary.title: Day 2: Tbilisi – Jvari – Mtskheta – Ananuri – Stepantsminda (Kazbegi)
itinerary.content:
North today, up the old Georgian Military Highway into the Caucasus. First stop is Mtskheta, Georgia's spiritual heart — the great Svetitskhoveli cathedral in the town, and Jvari monastery on the hill above it, both UNESCO sites. Then a pause at Ananuri, a fortress standing over the turquoise Jinvali reservoir, before the road climbs to Kazbegi, a small town under the snows of Mount Kazbek where the air changes completely.

  • Visit Jvari Monastery (UNESCO World Heritage Site);
  • Explore Mtskheta and Svetitskhoveli Cathedral;
  • Stop at Ananuri Architectural Complex;
  • Enjoy views of Jinvali Reservoir;
  • Arrive in Stepantsminda (Kazbegi);
  • Overnight stay in Kazbegi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 3.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 3: Kazbegi – Tsinandali – Telavi
itinerary.content:
An early start for Gergeti Trinity Church — the lone church on the hillside with Kazbek behind it, and the view most people come to Georgia for. It's best in the morning, before the cloud sets in. Then a long, scenic drive east into Kakheti, the wine country, with a stop at the old Tsinandali estate to taste in its gardens before settling into Telavi for the night.

  • Visit Gergeti Trinity Church with mountain views;
  • Depart Kazbegi for wine country;
  • Explore Tsinandali Estate and gardens;
  • Wine tasting experience;
  • Arrive in Telavi;
  • Overnight stay in Telavi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 4 hours

itinerary.title: Day 4: Telavi – Khareba Winery – Sighnaghi – Bodbe – Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
The full wine day. It starts at Khareba, where the cellar is a tunnel cut straight into the mountainside and the tasting happens deep inside. Then Sighnaghi, a small walled town of red roofs above the Alazani valley, and Bodbe, the quiet convent just below it. Back to Tbilisi in the evening for your last night.

  • Visit Khareba Winery (cave wine cellar);
  • Wine tasting experience;
  • Explore Sighnaghi, the "City of Love";
  • Visit Bodbe Monastery;
  • Scenic drive back to Tbilisi;
  • Overnight stay in Tbilisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 9-10 hours
  • Driving duration: 3.5 hours

Check out of your hotel by 12:00 p.m. When it's time, we'll transfer you to Tbilisi International Airport for your departure.

6-day-georgia-private-tour-highlights-fr.title: 6-Day Georgia Private Tour: Highlights from Tbilisi
6-day-georgia-private-tour-highlights-fr.seoTitle: 6-Day Georgia Private Tour: Highlights & Culture from Tbilisi
6-day-georgia-private-tour-highlights-fr.description:
Cave cities and cliff monasteries, in six days. This private loop runs west from Tbilisi through the heart of old Georgia — rock-hewn towns, a monastery dug into a mountainside, and two of the country's great medieval churches — before circling back to the capital.

You start in Tbilisi, then head west to the Iron Age caves of Uplistsikhe and the old spa town of Borjomi. From there it's up to Vardzia, a whole monastery carved into a cliff, and the rebuilt castle at Akhaltsikhe, before dropping down to Kutaisi and the green water of Martvili Canyon on the way home.

The thread running through it is stone — towns, churches and monasteries cut straight into the rock over the last three thousand years. Vardzia alone once held hundreds of rooms across up to thirteen levels, built into the mountain under Queen Tamar in the 12th century.

The days are full and the driving is real, but each evening lands you somewhere new — and because it's private, the whole thing bends around you rather than the other way round.

A week of Georgian culture, built around two cities. You spend three nights in Kutaisi, the old western capital, and three in Tbilisi, with the monasteries, cave towns and one big mountain day filling the space between.

Kutaisi comes first — its clifftop monasteries, the Green Bazaar, and the Prometheus Cave underground — before the drive east to Tbilisi. From the capital you head up the old Military Highway for a day at Kazbegi and the Gergeti church under Mount Kazbek, then work back west through the Uplistsikhe cave town and Gori to close the loop where it began.

The through-line is the old and the hand-carved: 12th-century Gelati on the UNESCO list, the rock-cut halls of Uplistsikhe, a lone church at 2,170 metres. Two of the days ask for real time on the road, but you unpack just twice, and since the tour runs only for your group, the route and pace stay open to change.

8-day-georgia-private-tour-culture-natur.description:
Mountains, monasteries and wine, in eight days. This private trip from Tbilisi runs up to the high Caucasus at Kazbegi, then out into the Kakheti wine country, using a few fixed bases so you're not packing and unpacking every night.

You start in the capital and drive north over the Georgian Military Highway to Kazbegi, spending two nights under Mount Kazbek for the church at Gergeti and the Gveleti waterfall. Coming back through the cave town of Uplistsikhe and Gori, you return to Tbilisi and swing east into Kakheti for two days of wineries, hill towns and old estates, with a free day in the capital to finish.

Wine is the through-line of the second half. Georgians have made it in buried clay qvevri for around 8,000 years, and in Kakheti you'll taste it where it's made — from a grand 19th-century estate to small family cellars.

Some days are long and the driving is real, but the mountains and the wine country are the two things most people come to Georgia for — and because it's private, the pace and the stops bend around you.

  • Tbilisi Botanical Garden – A peaceful green space in the heart of the city, ideal for a walk among plants, waterfalls, and scenic viewpoints.
  • Georgian National Museum – A great place to learn more about the country's history, archaeology, and culture.
  • Dry Bridge Market – A famous open-air flea market where you can find antiques, Soviet memorabilia, old cameras, and unique souvenirs.
  • Rustaveli Avenue – Tbilisi's main boulevard, lined with historic buildings, theatres, cafés, and shops.

9-day-georgia-private-tour-kutaisi-to-tb.description:
Nine days across Georgia, from the western lowlands up to the high Caucasus and back. You base yourself four nights in Kutaisi and three in Tbilisi, with one night high in the mountains at Kazbegi.

The loop runs Kutaisi first — its hillside monasteries and the Green Bazaar — then east through the Prometheus Cave to Tbilisi, and north up the old Military Highway to sleep a night below Mount Kazbek beneath the Gergeti church. Heading back you pass through Mtskheta, the Uplistsikhe cave town and Gori, saving the quieter west for last.

That final day is the one shorter tours leave out: Nokalakevi, a fortress ruin known as the "Georgian Troy," and the green water of Martvili Canyon. It's an unhurried take on the classic route, with a proper mountain overnight in place of a long day trip — and because you're travelling privately, none of it is fixed.

The full sweep of Georgia, coast to Caucasus, in nine days. This private tour runs from Tbilisi west and south through the country's best — old capitals, cave cities, a cliff monastery — and out to Batumi on the Black Sea before looping back.

You start with two nights in Tbilisi, then head west through the UNESCO churches of Mtskheta, the cave town of Uplistsikhe and Gori to Kutaisi, with its great monastery and the Prometheus Cave. From there it's south to Vardzia and the castle at Akhaltsikhe, then over to the coast at Batumi for two nights, and the long drive back to the capital.

It's the grand tour — the one that strings the country's headline sights into a single loop. Vardzia alone is a whole monastery carved into a cliff under Queen Tamar in the 12th century; Batumi, at the other end, is all sea air, palm-lined boulevard and glass towers.

A couple of the driving days are long, but that's the trade for seeing this much of the country in one trip — and because it's private, the pace and the stops bend around you.

9-day-georgia-wine-and-adventure-tour.description:
Wine and the high Caucasus, in nine days. This private tour pairs Georgia's big mountains with its oldest wine region, run from three easy bases so the driving stays manageable.

You settle into Tbilisi first, with a city day and a run out to the UNESCO churches of Mtskheta and the Ananuri fortress. Then it's north into the Caucasus for three nights at Kazbegi — the church at Gergeti, the Gudauri viewpoints, the Truso valley — before turning to Kakheti for the wine: tastings, the hill town of Sighnaghi, Telavi and the great Alaverdi cathedral.

The wine is the other half of the trip. Georgians have made it in buried clay qvevri for around 8,000 years, and in Kakheti you taste it where it's made, in a landscape of vineyards under the mountains.

A free day back in Tbilisi rounds it off. One or two days carry some real driving, but each leg lands somewhere different — and because it's private, the pace and the stops bend around you.

  • Dry Bridge Market – A famous open-air flea market where you can find antiques, Soviet memorabilia, old cameras, and unique souvenirs.

georgia-in-10-days-where-every-corner-ha.title: Georgia in 10 Days: Where Every Corner Has a Story and Every Meal is a Celebration
georgia-in-10-days-where-every-corner-ha.description:
The whole country in ten days, mountains to sea. This private tour runs a big loop from Tbilisi — the high Caucasus at Kazbegi, the cave cities and monasteries of the centre and west, and the Black Sea at Batumi — with a scenic train ride to close it out.

You start in the capital, head north to Kazbegi for two nights under the peaks, then work west through Gori and Uplistsikhe to Kutaisi, with its monasteries, the Prometheus Cave and Martvili Canyon. From there it's down to Batumi on the coast for two nights, and a relaxed train back to Tbilisi.

As the name says, the food is half the trip. Georgian cooking shifts as you cross the country — from the smoky mountain fare of the Caucasus to the walnut-and-herb dishes of the west and the coast — with wine that goes back some 8,000 years never far away.

A couple of the driving days are long, but each leg lands somewhere different — and because it's private, the pace and the stops bend around you.

itinerary.title: Day 1: Arrival and City Tour in Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
You'll be met at the airport and taken to your hotel. Check-in is from 14:00, so if you arrive earlier, we'll begin the city tour first and settle you in afterwards. Either way, the tour starts at Holy Trinity Cathedral — Sameba — one of the largest Orthodox churches in the world, rising above the city. From there you'll visit the clifftop Metekhi church, perched above the river, then ride the cable car up to the Narikala fortress for the view over the whole of Tbilisi. Walking down from the fortress, you'll pass through Abanotubani, the district of brick-domed sulfur bathhouses the city was built on and named after, then wander the Old Town lanes to the leaning clock tower of the Rezo Gabriadze theatre. After the tour, you'll have free time until the evening. The day ends with a welcome dinner of Georgian food and local wine.

  • Arrival in Tbilisi and hotel check-in;
  • Visit Holy Trinity Cathedral (Sameba);
  • See Metekhi Church;
  • Ride the cable car to Narikala Fortress;
  • Walk through the Abanotubani sulfur bath district;
  • See the Rezo Gabriadze Theatre clock tower;
  • Walk across the Peace Bridge;
  • Welcome dinner in Tbilisi;
  • Overnight stay in Tbilisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 4-5 hours
  • Driving duration: 30 minutes

itinerary.title: Day 2: Tbilisi – Jvari – Mtskheta – Ananuri – Stepantsminda (Kazbegi)
itinerary.content:
North today, up the old Georgian Military Highway into the Caucasus. First stop is Mtskheta, Georgia's spiritual heart — the great Svetitskhoveli cathedral in the town, and Jvari monastery on the hill above it, both UNESCO sites. Then a pause at Ananuri, a fortress standing over the turquoise Jinvali reservoir. Further up you'll stop where the black and white Aragvi rivers meet, their two colours running side by side before they blend into one, and again at the Gudauri Panorama for the wide view back down the valley. From there the road climbs to Kazbegi, a small town under the snows of Mount Kazbek where the air changes completely.

  • Visit Jvari Monastery (UNESCO World Heritage Site);
  • Explore Mtskheta and Svetitskhoveli Cathedral;
  • Stop at Ananuri Architectural Complex and enjoy views of Jinvali Reservoir;
  • See the confluence of Black and White Aragvi rivers;
  • Stop at Gudauri Panorama;
  • Overnight stay in Kazbegi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 3.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 3: Kazbegi – Gergeti Trinity Church – Gveleti Waterfalls – Dariali Gorge – Kazbegi
itinerary.content:
A day in the mountains around Kazbegi. The morning goes up to Gergeti Trinity, the lone church at 2,170 metres with Mount Kazbek behind it — best in the early light. Later you'll walk out to the Gveleti waterfalls, an easy hike of about an hour and a half there and back through the valley, and stop at the Dariali gorge near the Russian border, a dramatic cut in the mountains. Back in Kazbegi for the night.

  • Visit Gergeti Trinity Church;
  • Hike to the Gveleti Waterfalls (about 1.5 hours);
  • See the Dariali Gorge;
  • Overnight stay in Kazbegi.
  • Duration of the tour: 5-6 hours
  • Driving duration: 1.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 4: Kazbegi – Stalin Museum in Gori – Uplistsikhe – Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
You leave the mountains and head back down towards the centre of the country. First is Gori and its Stalin Museum, in the town where he was born — a place that has stayed largely unchanged since Soviet times. Then Uplistsikhe, a town carved straight into the rock thousands of years ago, its halls and tunnels still climbing the hillside. You reach Tbilisi in the evening.

  • Visit the Stalin Museum in Gori;
  • Visit Uplistsikhe cave town;
  • Overnight stay in Tbilisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 4 hours total

itinerary.title: Day 5: Tbilisi – Gelati – Motsameta – Kutaisi
itinerary.content:
West today, to Kutaisi, one of Georgia's oldest cities. On the way in you'll visit two monasteries: Gelati, founded in the 12th century and on the UNESCO list, its churches lined with medieval mosaics and frescoes, and the smaller Motsameta, perched on a cliff above a river bend. You settle into Kutaisi for the night.

  • Visit Motsameta Monastery;
  • Overnight stay in Kutaisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 7-8 hours
  • Driving duration: 4.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 6: Kutaisi – Prometheus Cave – Martvili Canyon – Kutaisi
itinerary.content:
A day of caves and canyons around Kutaisi. You'll go underground at the Prometheus Cave, a long run of lit chambers, stalactites and underground rivers, then out to Martvili Canyon, a narrow gorge of green water where a short boat trip takes you through the middle of it. An easy, scenic day, back in Kutaisi for the night.

  • Boat trip at Martvili Canyon;
  • Overnight stay in Kutaisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 3 hours

itinerary.content:
You head for the coast today, leaving Kutaisi for Batumi on the Black Sea. On the way you'll stop at a local winery for a tour and tasting — a chance to slow down over Georgian wine before the city. You arrive in Batumi, Georgia's seaside city, and settle in.

  • Driving duration: 2.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 8: Batumi City Tour
itinerary.content:
A relaxed day on the coast. You'll start north of the city at the Batumi Botanical Garden, a hillside of plants from all over the world spread across a green headland above the sea. Back in town, you'll take in Europe Square and the Italianate Piazza, then head down to the water for the moving Ali and Nino statue, two steel figures that slide through each other by the shore, and the Alphabetic Tower nearby, its tall helix wrapped in the letters of the Georgian alphabet. From there it's a stroll along the seafront Batumi Boulevard and a ride up on the Argo cable car for the view over the city and the coast. The evening is free.

georgias-wonders-11-day-grand-tour-from-.title: Georgia's Wonders: 11-Day Grand Tour from Kutaisi to Kazbegi and Batumi
georgias-wonders-11-day-grand-tour-from-.description:
Eleven days and most of Georgia — the caves and monasteries of the west, the Black Sea coast, the capital, and the high mountains. This grand loop settles you in four bases: four nights in Kutaisi, two in Batumi, two in Tbilisi and two at Kazbegi.

You start among Kutaisi's monasteries, the Prometheus Cave and the green water of Martvili Canyon, then drop to the sea at Batumi. From the coast a scenic train carries you east to Tbilisi, and the old Military Highway climbs north to two nights under Mount Kazbek and the Gergeti church. The way home turns back west through Gori and Uplistsikhe to Kutaisi.

It's the widest sweep of the shorter tours — canyon, coast, capital and Caucasus in one trip, with the Batumi train a pleasure in itself. The long legs carry some real driving, but four bases keep the packing down, and with your own guide-driver, the plan bends to suit you.

12-day-ultimate-georgia-adventure-tour-t.title: 12-Day Ultimate Georgia Adventure Tour: Tbilisi, Kazbegi, Mestia, Kutaisi, Batumi
12-day-ultimate-georgia-adventure-tour-t.description:
The big one — twelve days from the capital to the Black Sea, with the remote mountains of Svaneti in between. This private tour strings together nearly everything Georgia is known for: the high Caucasus at Kazbegi, the cave cities and monasteries of the centre and west, the tower villages of Svaneti, and the coast at Batumi.

You start in Tbilisi and head north to Kazbegi for the church at Gergeti, then work west through Gori and Uplistsikhe to Kutaisi, with its monasteries, the Prometheus Cave and Martvili Canyon. From there you climb into Svaneti for two nights in Mestia and a day out to Ushguli, before dropping to Batumi on the coast and taking the train back to the capital.

Svaneti is the heart of it — medieval stone towers under some of the highest peaks in the country, in a region that stayed cut off long enough to keep its own language and traditions. Getting there takes a long mountain drive, and it's worth every hour.

It's a full itinerary with some real driving days, but each leg lands somewhere genuinely different — and because it's private, the pace and the stops bend around you.

It opens in Kutaisi with its monasteries and the Prometheus Cave, then climbs into Svaneti for Mestia and Ushguli, where stone towers stand beneath Georgia's highest peaks. Back down, you stop at Martvili Canyon en route to Batumi and the sea, ride the train east to Tbilisi — with a free day to spend as you like — and close with the Military Highway up to Kazbegi and the Gergeti church before the long drive back to Kutaisi.

It's the fullest of the loops — lowland churches, alpine towers, canyon, coast and Caucasus in one trip. A few mountain drives run long, but five settled bases and a free day keep it unhurried, and since it's yours alone, you set the pace.

A few of the driving days are long, but each leg lands somewhere genuinely different — and because it's private, the pace and the stops bend around you.

The day starts with a walk through Telavi — the old town, the giant 900-year-old plane tree, and the Batonistsikhe castle, the former royal residence of the kings of Kakheti. Then out to the Tsinandali estate, the 19th-century home and gardens of Prince Alexander Chavchavadze, and a local winery where you get hands-on with a qvevri — the buried clay vessel Georgians have fermented wine in for millennia. A last stop in Vardisubani, known for its qvevri-making, before heading back to Telavi for the night.

  • Walk through Telavi and see the 900-year-old plane tree;
  • Visit Batonistsikhe Castle;
  • Visit Tsinandali Estate;
  • Qvevri winemaking at a local winery;
  • Visit Vardisubani;
  • Overnight stay in Telavi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 2 hours

itinerary.title: Day 5: Telavi – David Gareja Monastery – Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
Today you head south to David Gareja, a cave monastery cut into a bare hillside in the semi-desert near the Azerbaijani border. It's a striking, remote place — rock-hewn cells and chapels founded in the 6th century, in a landscape that looks nothing like the rest of Georgia. In the afternoon you drive back to Tbilisi for the night.

  • Visit David Gareja Monastery;
  • Overnight stay in Tbilisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 4 hours total

itinerary.title: Day 6: Tbilisi – Jvari – Mtskheta – Ananuri – Stepantsminda (Kazbegi)
itinerary.content:
North today, up the old Georgian Military Highway into the Caucasus. First stop is Mtskheta, Georgia's spiritual heart — the great Svetitskhoveli cathedral in the town, and Jvari monastery on the hill above it, both UNESCO sites. Then a pause at Ananuri, a fortress standing over the turquoise Jinvali reservoir. Further up you'll stop where the black and white Aragvi rivers meet, their two colours running side by side before they blend into one, and again at the Gudauri Panorama for the wide view back down the valley. From there the road climbs to Kazbegi, a small town under the snows of Mount Kazbek where the air changes completely.

  • Visit Jvari Monastery (UNESCO World Heritage Site);
  • Explore Mtskheta and Svetitskhoveli Cathedral;
  • Stop at Ananuri Architectural Complex and enjoy views of Jinvali Reservoir;
  • See the confluence of Black and White Aragvi rivers;
  • Stop at Gudauri Panorama;
  • Overnight stay in Kazbegi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 3.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 7: Kazbegi – Gergeti Trinity Church – Gveleti Waterfalls – Dariali Gorge – Kazbegi
itinerary.content:
The morning goes up to Gergeti Trinity, the lone church at 2,170 metres with Mount Kazbek behind it — best in the early light. Later you'll walk out to the Gveleti waterfalls, an easy hike of about an hour and a half there and back through the valley, and stop at the Dariali gorge near the Russian border, a dramatic cut in the mountains. Back in Kazbegi for the night.

  • Visit Gergeti Trinity Church;
  • Hike to the Gveleti Waterfalls (about 1.5 hours);
  • See the Dariali Gorge;
  • Overnight stay in Kazbegi.
  • Duration of the tour: 5-6 hours
  • Driving duration: 1.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 8: Kazbegi – Juta Village Trekking
itinerary.content:
Today is the hike. You head to Juta, a small village at the end of the road deep in the mountains, and trek up the valley beneath the sharp Chaukhi peaks — a walk of around five hours through alpine meadows, past clear streams and big open views. You stay the night in a local guesthouse, high up and far from anywhere.

  • Trek up the Juta valley beneath the Chaukhi peaks (about 5 hours);
  • Overnight stay in a Juta village guesthouse.
  • Duration of the tour: Full day trekking (about 5 hours on foot)

itinerary.title: Day 9: Juta Village – Kazbegi – Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
A last mountain morning at Juta before the long drive back. You'll come down through Kazbegi and retrace the Military Highway to Tbilisi, watching the Caucasus give way to the lowlands, and reach the capital in the evening.

  • Morning in Juta village;
  • Drive back to Tbilisi;
  • Overnight stay in Tbilisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 6-7 hours
  • Driving duration: 4 hours

itinerary.title: Day 10: Tbilisi – Bagrati Cathedral – Kutaisi
itinerary.content:
West today, to Kutaisi, one of Georgia's oldest cities, lived in for more than 3,000 years. Up on the hill sits Bagrati Cathedral, an 11th-century church rebuilt in recent years, looking out over the town. You settle into Kutaisi, your base for the western leg, for the night.

  • Visit Bagrati Cathedral;
  • Overnight stay in Kutaisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 7-8 hours
  • Driving duration: 4.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 11: Kutaisi – Gelati Monastery – Prometheus Cave
itinerary.content:
A day of monastery and cave. You'll start at Gelati, founded in the 12th century and on the UNESCO list, its churches lined inside with medieval mosaics and frescoes, then go underground at the Prometheus Cave, kilometres of lit chambers, stalactites and underground rivers. Back in Kutaisi for the night.

  • Visit Gelati Monastery (UNESCO World Heritage Site);
  • Visit Prometheus Cave;
  • Overnight stay in Kutaisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 2 hours

itinerary.title: Day 12: Kutaisi – Okatse Canyon – Martvili Canyon
itinerary.content:
A day of canyons. First is Okatse, where a walkway juts out over a deep gorge for a long, airy view down, then Martvili, a narrow canyon of green water with a short boat trip through the middle of it. An easy, scenic day out from Kutaisi, back in town for the night.

  • Visit Okatse Canyon;
  • Boat trip at Martvili Canyon;
  • Overnight stay in Kutaisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 3 hours

itinerary.title: Day 13: Kutaisi – Enguri Dam – Mestia
itinerary.content:
A long drive today takes you from Kutaisi up into Svaneti, the remote highland region in Georgia's northwest. On the way you'll make a short stop at the Enguri Dam, one of the highest arch dams in the world, for the view over the reservoir and the gorge below. From there the road climbs into the mountains to Mestia, the region's main town, set among medieval Svan towers under the peaks.

  • Stop at the Enguri Dam viewpoint;
  • See the Svan towers;
  • Overnight stay in Mestia.
  • Duration of the tour: 7-8 hours
  • Driving duration: 5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 14: Mestia – Ushguli – Mestia
itinerary.content:
A day out to Ushguli, a cluster of villages and one of the highest permanently inhabited places in Europe. The rough mountain road is half the experience, and at the top the stone towers stand under Mount Shkhara, Georgia's highest peak, with the little Lamaria church on the hillside above the village — a working chapel that has watched over Ushguli for centuries. Back in Mestia for the night.

  • Visit Ushguli;
  • See the Lamaria Church;
  • Overnight stay in Mestia.
  • Duration of the tour: 7-8 hours
  • Driving duration: 3 hours

itinerary.title: Day 15: Mestia – Koruldi Lakes – Mestia
itinerary.content:
A half-day up to the Koruldi Lakes, high on the ridge above Mestia. A 4WD vehicle takes you most of the way up the rough mountain track, and from the top it's a short walk to the little alpine lakes, with the great wall of the Caucasus — Ushba above all — spread out in front of you. It's one of the finest viewpoints in Svaneti, weather permitting. Back in Mestia for the night.

  • Drive up by 4WD towards the Koruldi Lakes;
  • Short walk to the Koruldi Lakes;
  • Overnight stay in Mestia.
  • Duration of the tour: 5-6 hours
  • Driving duration: 3 hours (by 4WD)

itinerary.title: Day 16: Mestia – Batumi
itinerary.content:
A long drive today takes you from the mountains all the way to the sea. You come down out of Svaneti and follow the coast road to Batumi, Georgia's Black Sea city — a complete change of scene after the highlands, and your base for the last few days.

  • Drive from Mestia to Batumi;
  • Overnight stay in Batumi.
  • Duration of the tour: 7-8 hours
  • Driving duration: 6 hours

itinerary.title: Day 17: Batumi City Tour
itinerary.content:
A relaxed day on the coast. You'll start north of the city at the Batumi Botanical Garden, a hillside of plants from all over the world spread across a green headland above the sea. Back in town, you'll take in Europe Square and the Italianate Piazza, then head down to the water for the moving Ali and Nino statue, two steel figures that slide through each other by the shore, and the Alphabetic Tower nearby, its tall helix wrapped in the letters of the Georgian alphabet. From there it's a stroll along the seafront Batumi Boulevard and a ride up on the Argo cable car for the view over the city and the coast. The evening is free.

  • Visit the Batumi Botanical Garden;
  • Walk through Europe Square and Piazza Square;
  • See the Ali and Nino statue;
  • See the Alphabetic Tower;
  • Walk along Batumi Boulevard;
  • Ride the Argo cable car;
  • Overnight stay in Batumi.
  • Duration of the tour: 5-6 hours
  • Driving duration: 1 hour

itinerary.title: Day 18: Batumi – Adjarian Cuisine Cooking Class
itinerary.content:
Today you cook. Adjara has its own take on Georgian food — above all the boat-shaped acharuli khachapuri, filled with cheese and topped with butter and an egg — and in a hands-on class you'll learn to make a few regional dishes before sitting down to eat them. The rest of the day is yours by the sea, a gentle close to the trip.

  • Adjarian cuisine cooking class;
  • Free time by the sea;
  • Overnight stay in Batumi.
  • Duration of the tour: 6-7 hours (cooking class)

itinerary.title: Day 19: Batumi – Tbilisi (Train)
itinerary.content:
Check out of your hotel by 12:00 p.m. At 16:00 you'll be transferred to Batumi Railway Station for the 16:50 train to Tbilisi — a scenic ride of about four hours across the country, arriving at 20:50. On arrival, you'll be transferred to your hotel for the night.

  • Check out of the hotel by 12:00 p.m.;
  • Transfer to Batumi Railway Station at 16:00;
  • Train from Batumi to Tbilisi (16:50–20:50);
  • Transfer to your hotel on arrival;
  • Overnight stay in Tbilisi.
  • Train ride: 4 hours

itinerary.title: Day 20: Departure from Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
Check out of your hotel by 12:00 p.m. When it's time, we'll transfer you to Tbilisi International Airport for your departure.

  • Hotel check-out by 12:00 p.m.;
  • Transfer to Tbilisi International Airport;
  • Departure.
  • Driving duration: 30 minutes
